ethiopia.content: KDF team detonates three RPG explosives near Kenya-Ethiopia border amid crisis - Hiiraan Online Jobs | Twitter | Somali Links | RSS Dark Mode Hiiraan Online HOME OPINION POLITICS RSS CONTACT US FACEBOOK × OPINION WARARKA MAANTA SPORTS SECURITY POLITICS Privacy Policy Contact Us Jobs advertisements HOME SECURITY KDF team detonates three RPG explosives near Kenya-Ethiopia border amid crisis Share Facebook Messenger Twitter WhatsApp LinkedIn Telegram Copy Link Email Font Size A- A A+ by CYRUS OMBATI Friday November 13, 2026 IG Kanja in Moyale A team of Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) personnel safely detonated three rocket-propelled grenades (RPGs) discovered near the Kenya-Ethiopia border in the Sessi area of Moyale, Marsabit County. The detonation was the second exercise in two weeks, officials said amid a growing crisis. The explosives, which had no visible registration markings, were destroyed on Monday, November 9, following reports that two RPGs had landed near a slaughter site close to the border. The two explosives, fitted with stabilising fins at the rear, were reportedly fired from Ethiopia at around 2 am Monday before landing a few metres inside Kenyan territory, officials said. KDF officers based in Moyale carried out the controlled demolition, with no injuries or property damage reported. advertisements On their way back from the demolition site, the soldiers discovered a third RPG along the roadside near Sessi Mixed Secondary School. The third explosive, which did not have stabilising fins, was also safely detonated. Authorities said they had increased security personnel in the area to address the growing crisis. The explosives are being launched by rival groups targeting those seeking refuge in Kenyan side. The government has confirmed that approximately 40,000 Ethiopians have crossed into Kenya and are currently being hosted in Moyale following escalating tensions in parts of Ethiopia. Prime Cabinet Secretary Musalia Mudavadi said tensions in Ethiopia had forced thousands of people to flee into Kenya. "The issue is that from the Ethiopian side, they have been having a little bit of tension over there. So, the problem has caused about 40,000 people to evacuate to Kenya," he said. Mudavadi said he had communicated with his Ethiopian counterpart and asked him to intervene and help stabilise the situation so that the displaced families can return home. "I told him to try and calm the situation in their country so that the refugees return to their homes," he said. He added that the Ethiopian government had assured Kenya that it was working to restore normalcy. "They have assured us that they will do their best to return the issues to normalcy and then the people can go back," Mudavadi said. The displacement follows clashes that erupted in October 2026, amid longstanding disagreements between the Oromia and Somali regional administrations over territorial boundaries and administrative control. The fighting has displaced thousands of people, with many families seeking shelter in schools, churches and temporary camps, while others have been accommodated by relatives and members of the local community. Inspector General of Police Douglas Kanja ordered the deployment of additional police officers to Moyale, Marsabit County, amid growing security concerns linked to developments in neighbouring Ethiopia. Kanja announced the reinforcement on November 5, during a security assessment visit to the border town, where he chaired a strategic meeting with regional security commanders to review the prevailing security situation. He directed officers deployed in the area to remain on high alert and strengthen surveillance to protect residents and their property. The Inspector General assured residents that the National Police Service (NPS) was committed to maintaining peace and stability in the region through enhanced security operations. “We are here to ensure all the visitors and locals are safe. We will ensure more personnel arrive for protection,” he said. He also urged members of the public to cooperate with security agencies by providing timely and relevant information that could help prevent security threats. Kanja toured a camp hosting families displaced by insecurity, where he assured them of enhanced protection and coordinated humanitarian assistance in partnership with relief agencies. The security assessment comes amid concerns over instability in neighbouring Ethiopia and its potential implications for security along Kenya's northern border. Kanja was accompanied by Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI) Director Mohammed Amin, General Service Unit (GSU) Commandant Johanna Tonui and Kenya Police Service Director of Operations Philip Opiyo. Others present included Eastern Regional Commissioner Jacob Muganda, Eastern Regional Police Commander Stephen Chebet, Eastern Regional Administration Police Commander Michael Owino and Regional Criminal Investigations Officer Michael Sang, alongside other senior security officials. The visit came a day after a 20-year-old woman was seriously injured after being struck by two suspected stray bullets believed to have originated from neighbouring Ethiopia in Moyale, Marsabit County. The incident occurred on November 4, 2026, at approximately 12:15pm while the victim was at her home in Biashara area. Police said she was hit by two bullets in the back, leaving her unconscious. She was rushed to Taqwa Nursing Home Hospital, where medical personnel removed the two bullets. The victim was admitted in serious condition as police documented the incident. The circumstances under which the bullets crossed into Kenyan territory remain unclear. This is the latest such incident in the area amid growing crisis due to ongoing fighting in Ethiopia pitting two communities. A 65-year-old woman was killed in the area, after she was reportedly struck by a suspected stray bullet believed to have originated from ongoing clashes in neighbouring Ethiopia. The deceased was identified as Amina Guchi, who was reportedly at the Moyale County offices, located next to Moyale Law Courts, when the incident occurred on November 2, 2026. Guchi was speaking to a security official on duty when an object believed to be a stray bullet struck her on the head from behind. She collapsed and lost consciousness before being rushed to Moyale Sub-County Referral Hospital, where she was pronounced dead on arrival. Police officers subsequently visited the hospital, where a post-mortem examination was conducted before the body was released to the family for burial arrangements. The neighbouring Moyale is experiencing conflict which has displaced more than 50,000 people. Security officers in the area had earlier on safely detonated three rocket-propelled grenades (RPGs) that reportedly landed in the area after being discharged from neighbouring Ethiopia. The explosives were discovered on Sunday, November 1, 2026, following a report about unexploded explosive materials that had landed near Sessi Primary School. This affected learning and examinations at the centre. Two Kenya Certificate of Secondary Education (KCSE) examination centres in Moyale Sub-County, Marsabit County, were relocated following the insecurity linked to clan clashes along the Kenya-Ethiopia border. According to police, the explosives were found at two locations- one at Sessi Primary School and two others at the Meteorological Department offices. Police and a team of bomb disposal experts from the Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) based at Odha rushed to the scene. The security team established that the materials were three RPGs, which were subsequently secured, removed and safely detonated by the bomb experts. At least three people had been injured after bullets hit structures in the area two weeks ago. The United Nations refugee agency has warned of growing humanitarian needs in northern Kenya after an estimated 50,000 people fled clashes in Ethiopia and crossed the border into Moyale in search of safety. The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) said significant cross-border movements had been reported since October 22, with the number of arrivals remaining fluid as registration and verification efforts continued. Local authorities estimate that up to 50,000 people have entered Kenya, with reports indicating that additional crossings could further increase the number of people requiring assistance. Many of those fleeing the violence are women and children, raising concerns over their protection and access to essential services. The conflict started three weeks ago following the alleged raising of the flag of the Somali Regional State in Ethiopia, which triggered clashes between forces and groups from the Oromia and Somali regional states. According to UNHCR, some arrivals are staying with relatives and host communities, while others have sought temporary shelter in schools and churches. EST to November 13 at 9:00 A.M. EST. To receive the Africa File, Ethiopia War Security Review, or Congo War Security Review via email, please subscribe here . Follow CTP on X , LinkedIn , and BlueSky for daily updates. Read CTP’s latest analysis on the war in Ethiopia in the weekly Africa File here . Key Takeaways: Northern Axis. Local sources claimed that Amhara Fano National Movement fighters fought alongside Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) forces against Ethiopian federal forces near the Ethiopia-Eritrea border, although the Critical Threats Project (CTP) could not confirm the unverified claims. Western Axis. The Ethiopian military reportedly sustained fighting with TPLF and Eritrean forces around Badme, an Eritrean border town. Central Axis. Ethiopian federal and TPLF forces reportedly clashed in the mountainous Tigray interior south of Axum. Major Domestic Political Developments. The interim Tigray regional government has continued setting up its administration amid internal tensions. Ethiopian security forces are reportedly conducting forced conscription in the Oromia region and Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian capital. Regional and International Activity. Various international actors affirmed their support for de-escalation between Ethiopia and Eritrea, although officials from the two countries have continued to accuse each other of escalation. Figure 1. ENDF and TPLF Battle Across Tigray Note: ENDF stands for Ethiopian National Defense Force. TPLF stands for Tigray People’s Liberation Front. Source: Michael DeAngelo; Liam Karr; Alexander Brown. Eastern Axis: Afar Region Nothing significant to report. Northern Axis: Rama-Zalambessa-Dallol Local sources claimed that Amhara Fano National Movement (AFNM) fighters fought alongside the Tigray Defense Force (TDF), the TPLF’s military wing, against Ethiopian federal forces near the Ethiopia-Eritrea border, although CTP could not confirm the unverified claims. Federal and TDF forces reportedly clashed around Rama, which is approximately 20 miles north of Adwa and just south of the Ethiopia-Eritrea border, on November 7. [1] Armed Conflict Location & Event Data (ACLED) reported that federal forces retook Rama, while the TDF claimed to have overcome federal forces and inflicted mass casualties upon them. [2] Fighting between the two sides reportedly broke out again around Rama between November 9 and 11. [3] The Ethiopian news outlet Wazema Radio cited residents who claimed that the AFNM and Afar Revolutionary Democratic Unity Front—both of whom are members of the Alliance for Survival rebel coalition with the TPLF—fought alongside the TDF. [4] Conflict tracker Sajid Nadeem and another conflict tracker on X also reported that the AFNM participated in the fighting, although CTP could not confirm the unverified claims. [5] Western Axis: Humera-Addi Remets-Shire The Ethiopian military (Ethiopian National Defense Force, ENDF) reportedly sustained fighting with TDF and Eritrean forces around Badme, an Eritrean border town. The ENDF reportedly began fighting with TDF and Eritrean forces around the town on November 9 following several days of mutual buildups, although CTP could not verify whether fighting occurred on the Ethiopian or Eritrean side of the border. [6] Wazema Radio and a conflict tracker on X reported that the ENDF and TDF continued clashing on November 10 near Gomahalo, which is an Ethiopian village approximately 20 miles south of Badme. [7] The ENDF and Eritrean military (Eritrean Defense Forces, EDF) reportedly traded artillery fire around Badme from November 11 to 13. [8] The EDNF also reportedly conducted drone strikes on EDF positions. [9] The Ethiopian Conflict Map and Sajid Nadeem claimed that the ENDF captured Badme on November 12, although ACLED reported on November 13 that neither the ENDF nor the EDF controlled the town but that “Eritrean intelligence personnel” had been present. [10] The Ethiopian news outlet Addis Standard cited a resident of Badme who said that ENDF forces have been present in Badme since November 12, however. [11] Central Axis: Abiy Addi-Adwa-Axum Ethiopian federal forces and the TDF reportedly clashed in the mountainous Tigray interior south of Axum. The TDF has contested Ethiopian federal efforts to control areas around Tigray’s city belt since mid-October 2026. [12] The Ethiopian Conflict Map and Sajid Nadeem reported that the two sides clashed near Semema, which is approximately 20 miles south of Axum, on November 11. [13] Southern Axis: Mekele-Alamata-Sekota-Woldia Nothing significant to report. Northern Amhara Sector: From B21 Northward Nothing significant to report. Other Rebel Kinetic Activity Nothing significant to report. Major Domestic Political Developments The interim Tigray regional government has continued setting up its administration amid internal tensions. The interim administration has reportedly faced discord over appointments and governance, including payment of civil servants’ salaries. [14] A conflict tracker on X reported on November 11 that 11 senior members of Ethiopian Prime Ministerial Adviser Getachew Reda’s Simret party, which heavily influences the interim administration, resigned due to the discord. [15] Two conflict trackers separately reported on November 10 that the interim administration appointed Daniel Negash as “coordinator” for the Western Zone, which is disputed by Amhara and Tigrayan communities. [16] Ethiopian security forces are reportedly conducting forced conscription in the Oromia region and Addis Ababa. The Ethiopian Human Rights Commission and Addis Standard previously reported on forced conscription in Oromia in at least December 2024 and August 2026, respectively. [17] Addis Standard and the Canadian news outlet The Globe and Mail cited residents of Oromia and Addis Ababa on November 12 who reported that Ethiopian security forces had forcibly conscripted some of their family members and other civilians. [18] The Globe and Mail cited two residents of Addis Ababa who separately reported that the ENDF had sent their sons to the front lines in Tigray. [19] Addis Standard cited residents of Jimma, one of the largest cities in Oromia, who described forced conscription as a factor that sparked protests against regional and federal authorities on November 9 and 10. [20] Regional and International Activity Various international actors affirmed their support for de-escalation between Ethiopia and Eritrea, although officials from the two countries have continued to accuse each other of escalation. Five Democratic members of the US Senate Foreign Relations Committee sent a letter to US Secretary of State Marco Rubio on November 10 that urged Rubio to increase US efforts to mediate between Ethiopia, Ethiopian rebel groups, and Eritrea. [21] The Democratic senators requested that the US State Department avoid offering Eritrea’s port of Assab to Ethiopia in any mediation and discourage Egypt, Eritrea, and Sudan from supporting Ethiopian rebel groups. [22] The Group of Seven (G7) foreign ministers separately released a statement on November 11 after meeting in Paris that expressed “great concern” over tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea and called for “maximum restraint” and “diplomatic solutions.” [23] Special Envoy of the United Nations (UN) Secretary-General for the Horn of Africa Guang Cong met with Getachew on November 11 to discuss the security situation in the Horn of Africa. Cong has previously pledged that the UN will work toward peace and stability in the region. [24] Ethiopian and Eritrean officials have continued to accuse each other of escalation, which has been a pattern since the renewed war in northern Ethiopia began in late September 2026. Getachew posted on X that he discussed the “destructive role the Regime in Asmara is playing in the region” during his meeting with Cong. [25] Getachew also directly accused Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki and Sudanese Transitional Sovereignty Council President Abdel Fattah al Burhan of equipping, arming, and coordinating with Ethiopian rebel groups, including by helping them conduct drone attacks in Ethiopia. [26] Eritrean Information Minister Yemane Gebremeskel posted on X on November 11 that Ethiopia has a “regional” war agenda. [27] The Eritrean Ministry of Information published an editorial on November 12 that accused Ethiopia of invading Eritrea. (Photo by Mohamed Khidir/Xinhua) KHARTOUM, Nov. 13 (Xinhua) -- Relations between Sudan and Ethiopia have entered a new phase of tension, as mutual accusations of interference in internal affairs and support for armed groups have spilled over into diplomatic retaliation and appeals to international and regional bodies. The growing rift has raised concerns over its potential implications for stability in the Horn of Africa. The Sudanese government has accused Ethiopia of allowing its territory to be used as a launching ground for drones targeting Sudan and providing logistical support to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which have been fighting the Sudanese Armed Forces since April 2023. Khartoum has filed complaints with the UN Security Council and the African Union Peace and Security Council, accusing Addis Ababa of facilitating attacks launched from Ethiopian territory. Ethiopia subsequently closed the Sudanese consulate in Asosa and gave six Sudanese diplomats 48 hours to leave the country. Sudan responded by closing the Ethiopian consulate in Gedaref and expelling its diplomats. Addis Ababa, meanwhile, accused Sudan of providing safe havens and logistical support to fighters from the Tigray People's Liberation Front, which has been engaged in a prolonged confrontation with the Ethiopian government. MUTUAL ACCUSATIONS DEEPEN SECURITY CONCERNS Khalid Dirar, a professor of political science at al-Rasid Center for Strategic Studies in Khartoum, said the diplomatic escalation reflected growing tensions and could lead to further restrictions on official relations. Beyond the diplomatic dispute, the mutual accusations reflect deeper security concerns and competing regional interests, said the observers. Ethiopian political analyst Biniam Niguse noted that Addis Ababa viewed the Sudanese army's repeated accusations and Khartoum's involvement in a regional axis as attempts to encircle Ethiopia and exert pressure on it. Whatever the motives behind them, the recent exchange of accusations reflects growing mistrust between the two countries, with both increasingly concerned about threats to their respective security and political interests. Sudanese political analyst Abdul-Raziq Ziyada warned that the conflicts in Sudan and Ethiopia could become increasingly intertwined, with repercussions extending to neighboring countries. Continued tensions could undermine border security, disrupt population movements and trade, and create opportunities for armed groups to conduct cross-border activities, Niguse cautioned. This photo taken on March 6, 2026 shows an equestrian statue in Mekelle, Tigray region, Ethiopia. (Xinhua/Liu Fangqiang) LONGSTANDING DISPUTES COMPLICATE BILATERAL TIES The current crisis is also rooted in longstanding disagreements over the Fashaga border area, Nile waters and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam. Ziyada identified the dam and border disputes, particularly over Fashaga, as major sources of tension. The area is strategically important for agriculture and is home to communities with overlapping economic and social interests on both sides of the border. Ethiopian political expert Getachew Abra said Sudan's position on the Renaissance Dam was a source of concern for Addis Ababa. He noted that the dispute had expanded beyond water management to encompass broader political and security considerations. Abra also linked the current tensions to the repercussions of the conflict in the Tigray region, particularly after Sudan strengthened its presence in border areas. He noted that RSF accusations that Tigrayan fighters were participating alongside the Sudanese army had added another dimension to the dispute. He added that Ethiopia's internal conflicts and security challenges had further complicated its relations with neighboring countries. The overlapping conflicts in the two countries, particularly in border areas where armed groups operate, risk turning the shared frontier into a source of insecurity. This photo taken on April 16, 2025 shows the damage to Khartoum Hospital as a result of military clashes between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), in Khartoum, Sudan. (Photo by Mohamed Hamid/Xinhua) MILITARY CONFRONTATION RISKS WIDER CONFLICT Analysts have cautioned that the diplomatic dispute could potentially develop into a direct military confrontation, with implications extending beyond the two countries. In an analysis entitled "Sudan and Ethiopia: A New Front of Confrontation in a Dangerous Situation," the International Center for Strategic Studies warned that any Sudanese military response targeting sites inside Ethiopia, including airports or drone launch facilities, could widen the conflict and turn it into a regional confrontation. Ziyada similarly cautioned that attacks on military sites or facilities inside either country could trigger reciprocal military measures that would be difficult to contain, particularly amid the ongoing conflict in Sudan and overlapping regional interests and alliances. Such escalation could further destabilize the Horn of Africa, where the conflicts in Sudan and Ethiopia intersect with Nile water disputes and competition among regional powers. Addressing border security and non-interference in internal affairs, while maintaining political and diplomatic communication, were essential to containing the crisis and safeguarding stability across the Horn of Africa, Ziyada said. ■ Comments Comments (0) Send You may like Miao ethnic group celebrates Miao New Year in SW China's Guizhou Media center for 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Week opens in Shenzhen, China's Guangdong Top honors unveiled at China's Golden Rooster Awards Highlights of cultural events at 9th CIIE Shenzhen Int'l Garden and Flower Expo Park reopens after renovations 9th China International Import Expo concludes in Shanghai More from GLOBALink Experts highlight APEC's role in boosting regional cooperation, trade stability China's green development wins praise at COP31 An American man's decades-long bond with a Chinese county Follow us on More from GLOBALink Experts highlight APEC's role in boosting regional cooperation, trade stability China's green development wins praise at COP31 An American man's decades-long bond with a Chinese county Follow us on World Insights: Sudan-Ethiopia tensions escalate amid mutual accusations, raising regional concerns
ethiopia.summary: Tensions between Sudan and Ethiopia have escalated significantly, marked by mutual accusations of interference in each other's internal affairs and support for armed groups. Sudan has accused Ethiopia of allowing drone attacks against its territory and aiding the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which have been in conflict with the Sudanese Armed Forces since April 2023. In response, Sudan has lodged complaints with the UN Security Council and the African Union, while Ethiopia has expelled Sudanese diplomats and closed its consulate in Asosa. The situation is further complicated by longstanding disputes over the Fashaga border area and the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam, which have historically strained relations. Analysts warn that these tensions could lead to military confrontations, potentially destabilizing the Horn of Africa. The overlapping conflicts and security concerns in both nations highlight the urgent need for diplomatic dialogue to prevent further escalation and ensure regional stability.

Speaking at a briefing on Ethiopia's participation in the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye, Billene highlighted the country's progress in environmental protection, renewable energy expansion and preparations to host COP32 in 2027. She disclosed that Ethiopia has planted more than 56 billion seedlings over the past eight years under the Green Legacy Initiative. The Press Secretary described this the flagship national programme as a major contribution to global efforts to mitigate climate change and restore degraded ecosystems. Follow us on WhatsApp | LinkedIn for the latest headlines Billene stressed, however, that the initiative's success should not be measured by the number of seedlings planted alone, but also by their survival, continued care and protection to ensure lasting environmental benefits. She called for broader public participation in environmental conservation, emphasizing that nurturing and protecting planted trees must become a shared responsibility across all sections of society. She also recalled Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's repeated calls for citizens to take an active role in caring for planted trees to maximize their long-term environmental and economic benefits. Turning to Ethiopia's clean energy transition, Billene highlighted the country's expanding investments in hydropower, wind and solar energy to meet growing domestic electricity demand while strengthening its capacity to supply power to regional markets. She cited ongoing wind and solar projects as evidence of Ethiopia's efforts to diversify its renewable energy mix and advance a sustainable energy future. The Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD), she added, represents a major milestone in the country's renewable energy ambitions and electricity generation capacity. The landmark project will also be showcased at the Ethiopian Pavilion during COP31, she pointed out. Billene underscored that Ethiopia's investments in renewable energy, afforestation and environmental protection go beyond domestic development priorities, contributing to broader international efforts to address climate change and promote sustainable development. The briefing also highlighted Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's engagements at COP31, Ethiopia's preparations to host COP32 in 2027, and the country's plans to present its development achievements and climate action initiatives to the international community. The inhabitants further emphasized the need for consolidating progress toward lasting peace, stability and prosperity in the region. The call was made during a consultative forum of Mekelle residents, presided over by Chief of Staff of the Ethiopian National Defense Force (ENDF), Field Marshal Birhanu Jula. Keep up with the latest headlines on WhatsApp | LinkedIn Speaking at the gathering, Field Marshal Birhanu said the defunct TPLF faction had aligned itself with the so-called "Tsimdo" group, an alliance orchestrated by Ethiopia's historical adversaries to wage war against the country. He said his engagement with residents was aimed at fostering dialogue, strengthening cooperation and encouraging collective efforts to ensure lasting peace and stability in Tigray region. During the discussions, residents underscored their strong desire to see an end to conflict, identifying peace, security and sustainable development as their foremost priorities. They called for the reconstruction of damaged infrastructure, expanded employment opportunities for young people and the restoration of security to enable communities to resume normal life without fear. "Our foremost priorities are the reconstruction of critical infrastructure, the creation of meaningful employment opportunities for our youth, and the restoration of security so that citizens can go about their daily lives in peace," participants said. Residents also welcomed the resumption of salary payments for civil servants and ongoing infrastructure rehabilitation efforts, describing them as important steps toward restoring normalcy and accelerating the region's recovery. Concluding the forum, participants called on the Federal Government to maintain its commitment to Tigray, sustain ongoing interventions and accelerate reform, reconstruction and development initiatives to secure lasting peace and improve the livelihoods of communities across the region. (Reuters Photo) Mogadishu (HOL) — Türkiye's Ministry of National Defence has denied reports that it plans to deploy 15,000 troops to Somalia at the request of the federal government, reaffirming its commitment to military training and counterterrorism cooperation with Mogadishu. Speaking at a news briefing Thursday, ministry spokesperson Rear Adm. Zeki Aktürk rejected claims circulating in Turkish and Somali media about a large-scale deployment of Turkish forces to Somalia. “Claims that Türkiye will send 15,000 troops to Somalia at the request of the Somali government do not reflect the truth,” the ministry said. advertisements Aktürk confirmed that Türkiye already maintains a military presence in Somalia through the Somali-Turkish Task Force and an air component command. He said Turkish forces would continue supporting Somalia's counterterrorism capabilities through military assistance, training and advisory services. The denial follows reports suggesting that Somalia had sought additional military assistance from international partners, including Türkiye, amid concerns about security as African Union troop-contributing countries prepare to withdraw some of their forces. Some reports also alleged that fighters from Syrian armed groups involved in the overthrow of the former Syrian government could be deployed to Somalia. Those claims have not been substantiated. Türkiye operates the TURKSOM military training facility in Mogadishu, where Turkish instructors have trained Somali military personnel as part of efforts to strengthen the Somali National Army. adinsideThe facility, which opened in 2017, has played a significant role in developing Somalia's military capabilities, including training specialized units involved in operations against al-Shabab. The Turkish statement comes days after Turkish Ambassador to Somalia Ferhat Alkan met Somali National Security Adviser Aweys Haji Yusuf Ahmed in Mogadishu to discuss military cooperation, counterterrorism operations and regional security developments. During Tuesday's meeting, the two officials reviewed Somalia's security situation and efforts to strengthen cooperation between the countries as African Union forces prepare for changes to their deployments. “Türkiye continues to contribute to the peace, stability and security of Somalia, as it has in the past,” the Turkish Embassy said following the meeting. According to Somalia's Office of the National Security Adviser, the discussions also covered political developments, operations against al-Shabab and broader bilateral cooperation. The office said Somalia appreciated Türkiye's longstanding support and emphasized the importance of continued coordination to strengthen national security. The discussions come amid uncertainty over the future of the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia (AUSSOM), particularly following Uganda's announcement that it would withdraw troops deployed under bilateral arrangements and gradually end its participation in the mission. Uganda has been one of the largest contributors to African Union military operations in Somalia since 2007, playing a major role in securing Mogadishu and supporting operations against al-Shabab. The withdrawal plans have raised concerns about the readiness of Somali forces to assume responsibility for areas previously secured by foreign troops. Somalia and Türkiye maintain a longstanding defense partnership covering military training, counterterrorism, maritime security and military capacity-building. Despite rejecting reports of an additional 15,000 troops, Ankara reaffirmed that its existing military mission would continue supporting Somalia's efforts to strengthen its armed forces and combat militant groups. The agreement was signed in Antalya, Türkiye, on the sidelines of the COP31 United Nations climate conference by Somalia's Minister of Family and Human Rights Development, Khadija Mohamed Al-Makhzoumi, and Türkiye's Minister of Family and Social Services, Mahinur Özdemir Göktaş. advertisements According to Somalia's Ministry of Family and Human Rights Development, the agreement establishes a framework for cooperation in developing social welfare policies, exchanging expertise and strengthening services for vulnerable communities. The agreement covers the protection of women's and children's rights, prevention of violence against women and measures to safeguard children from risks associated with digital platforms and online environments. It also provides for cooperation in improving health and education services, along with care and rehabilitation programs for persons with disabilities and older people. The two governments agreed to organize training programs, conferences and seminars to strengthen the skills of social service professionals and facilitate the exchange of knowledge and experience. “The agreement is an important step toward improving Somalia's social services,” Al-Makhzoumi added, saying the government hopes to benefit from the experience of international partners, particularly Türkiye, in strengthening family protection and safeguarding the rights of women and children. The Somali minister also addressed a side event at COP31 focusing on the relationship between climate change, social protection and women's empowerment. She said recurring droughts and floods have severely affected Somali families, particularly women and children, who face increasing hardship as climate-related disasters disrupt livelihoods and access to essential services. Al-Makhzoumi called for international climate financing to reach the most vulnerable communities, especially rural families disproportionately affected by droughts and flooding. She also emphasized the importance of including women in the development of climate policies and adaptation strategies, highlighting their role in strengthening community resilience. The agreement comes as Somalia seeks greater international cooperation to improve social services and expand protection for communities affected by humanitarian emergencies and climate-related disasters. Türkiye has been one of Somalia's closest international partners since President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan visited Mogadishu in 2011 during a devastating drought and famine. Since then, Ankara has provided humanitarian assistance and supported projects in education, healthcare, infrastructure and institutional development. The two countries have also expanded cooperation in defense, military training, maritime security and energy development. The latest agreement broadens that relationship by placing greater emphasis on social welfare, family protection and support for vulnerable populations. (AP Photo/Abdel Kareem Hana) Mogadishu (HOL) — Somalia has joined 17 other Arab and Islamic countries in condemning an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in southern Gaza, urging Israel to uphold the ceasefire, protect civilians and allow unrestricted humanitarian assistance into the Palestinian territory. In a joint statement issued Saturday, Nov. 14, the foreign ministers of the 18 countries said the strike on the hospital in Khan Younis caused casualties among patients and medical personnel and violated international humanitarian law, which provides special protection for healthcare facilities and workers. advertisements The statement was signed by the foreign ministers of Somalia, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait, Oman, Egypt, Jordan, Sudan, Libya, Palestine, Djibouti, Algeria, Lebanon, Mauritania, Türkiye, Pakistan and Indonesia. The ministers also condemned continued Israeli attacks on Palestinian civilians, including strikes on tents and other shelters housing displaced families. They warned that the attacks threaten the Gaza ceasefire and undermine international efforts to restore security and stability in the territory. The joint statement expressed serious concern over Israeli restrictions on humanitarian assistance, including essential medical supplies and shelter materials such as tents, caravans and mobile homes. The ministers said the restrictions were worsening Gaza's humanitarian crisis as winter approaches, leaving displaced families exposed to harsh weather conditions. They warned that inadequate shelter, deteriorating sanitation facilities and limited access to clean water and healthcare were placing civilians at serious risk, particularly children and infants. The foreign ministers called on Israel to immediately and fully implement its commitments under the Sharm el-Sheikh agreement, U.S. President Donald Trump's comprehensive peace plan and United Nations Security Council Resolution 2803 of 2025. They urged Israel to maintain the ceasefire, protect civilians and medical facilities, and ensure the safe, sustained and unrestricted delivery of humanitarian aid in sufficient quantities. The statement also called for the entry of equipment and supplies needed to restore essential infrastructure and support early recovery efforts in Gaza. The ministers emphasized that humanitarian assistance should not be delayed by political or security conditions or made dependent on progress in subsequent phases of the peace agreement. “We call on Israel to allow United Nations agencies and humanitarian organizations to carry out their operations without obstruction,” they added. The countries urged the United States and the Board of Peace to intensify diplomatic efforts to ensure Israel fulfills its commitments and removes restrictions on humanitarian aid entering Gaza. The ministers reaffirmed their determination to work with regional and international partners to strengthen the ceasefire, implement all phases of the peace plan and expand humanitarian assistance to Palestinians affected by the conflict. Somalia has repeatedly expressed support for Palestinian rights and joined Arab and Islamic countries in calling for an end to attacks on civilians and greater humanitarian access to Gaza. The two-day meeting, which concluded Thursday, Nov. 12, brought together representatives from IGAD member states, the organization's secretariat and experts from the Conflict Early Warning and Response Mechanism (CEWARN). advertisements Somalia's Permanent Secretary, Hamza Adan Haadow, officially closed the meeting, which focused on strengthening regional cooperation in conflict early warning, prevention and coordinated responses to emerging security threats. Participants discussed ways to improve the identification of potential conflicts and strengthen collaboration among member states to address security challenges before they escalate. The meeting also highlighted the importance of sharing early warning information and coordinating responses to conflicts affecting communities across the Horn of Africa. CEWARN, an IGAD mechanism established to support conflict prevention, works with member states to monitor indicators of instability, assess potential risks and facilitate timely responses. Somalia's hosting of the committee for the first time reflects its growing participation in regional initiatives aimed at promoting peace, stability and security. The meeting comes as countries in the Horn of Africa continue to face security challenges, including armed conflicts, political instability and competition over natural resources. IGAD provides a regional platform for cooperation on peace and security, economic integration and development among its member states. somalia.summary: Ghanaian midfielder Thomas Partey is expected to miss the upcoming international match against Somalia due to the recent passing of his father. Partey, who plays for Arsenal in the English Premier League, is currently in Ghana to attend his father's funeral, which has understandably taken precedence over his football commitments. The Ghana Football Association (GFA) has expressed its condolences to Partey and his family during this difficult time. The absence of the experienced player is a significant loss for the Black Stars as they prepare for the crucial clash. Partey's contributions to the team have been invaluable, and his experience will be missed on the pitch. The GFA is likely to make adjustments to the squad in light of his absence, as they aim to secure a positive result in the match against Somalia. The team and fans alike will be hoping for a swift return for Partey once he has had the opportunity to grieve.

Qaraarka oo tirsigiisu yahay A/C.3/81/L.43 ayaa dalalka ugu baaqaya inay hakiyaan fulinta xukunnada dilka, iyadoo tallaabadaas loo arko waddo horseedi karta in mustaqbalka gebi ahaanba la joojiyo ciqaabtaas, iyadoo inta badan dalalka Islaamka ah ka aamuseen ama diideen marka laga yimaado Turkey, Somalia & Jabuti, halka Malaysia, Indonesia iyo Jordan ka gaabsadeen, waxaase qaraarkaan qaaddacay dalal ay kamid yihiin Mareykanka, Shiinaha, Itoobiya, Hindiya iyo Sacuudi Carabiya. Inkastoo ogolaanshaha qaraarkaani aysan ka dhignayn in Somalia laga mamnoocay fulinta qisaasta, iyadoo qaraarka ay ansixiyeen Guddiga Saddexaad weli uu u gudbi doono Golaha Guud ee Qaramada Midoobay si loo sii tixgeliyo. Posted by: Horseed Staff Dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa qaadacday dhaleecayn ay kala kulantay khubaro madax-bannaan oo ka tirsan Qaramada Midoobay, kuwaas… 15 November, 2026 Share Tweet Dowladda Soomaaliya ayaa qaadacday dhaleecayn ay kala kulantay khubaro madax-bannaan oo ka tirsan Qaramada Midoobay, kuwaas oo walaac ka muujiyay xil ka qaadistii lagu sameeyay Guddoomiyihii hore ee Maxkamadda Sare, Baashe Yuusuf Axmed iyo sax-ahaanshaha muddo kordhinta Madaxweynaha dalka. War-saxaafadeed kasoo baxay Wasaaradda Cadaaladda iyo Arrimaha Dastuurka ayaa lagu sheegay in khubarada Qaramada Midoobay ay baahiyeen warbixintooda iyaga oo aan marka hore dowladda ka dalban jawaab rasmi ah, tallaabadaasi oo ay Wasaaraddu ku tilmaantay mid ka hor imaanaysa habraacyada shaqo ee khubarada madaxa-bannaan ee Golaha Xuquuqul Insaanka QM, inkasta oo ay sheegtay inay qiimeyso doorka hay’adaha xuquuqul insaanka ee Qaramada Midoobay. Xiisadda ayaa salka ku haysa xil ka qaadistii 4-tii November lagu sameeyay Baashe Yuusuf Axmed, xilli Maxkamadda Sare ay gacanta ku haysay dacwad dastuuri ah oo la xiriirtay muddo xileedka Madaxweynaha Soomaaliya Xasan Sheekh Maxamuud, iyadoo maxkamaddu soo saartay go’aan ay ku burisay wax-ka-beddelkii dastuurka ee Madaxweynaha loogu kordhiyay muddo hal sano ah, iyadoo sidoo kale amartay in doorashooyinka federaalka lagu qabto muddo 90 maalmood gudahood ah. 12-kii November, khubarada Qaramada Midoobay ee Margaret Satterthwaite iyo Ben Saul ayaa dowladda Soomaaliya ugu baaqay inay dib xilka ugu soo celiso Baashe Yuusuf Axmed, iyagoo ku doodey in xil ka qaadistiisa aan loo marin habraacyadii dastuuriga ahaa, oo ay ku jiraan ansixinta Baarlamaanka iyo soo jeedinta Guddiga Adeegga Garsoorka. Dhinaca kale, Wasaaradda Cadaaladda ayaa difaacday habka xilka looga qaaday guddoomiyihii hore, iyadoo sheegtay in Golaha Sare ee Garsoorka, oo uu dhigayo Dastuurka cusub ee la ansixiyay bishii Maarso 2026, aanu weli dhismin. Sida ay wasaaraddu sheegtay xilkana looga qaaday hannaan la mid ah kii markii hore lagu magacaabay, iyadoo go’aanka lagu saleeyay nidaamkii ku-meel-gaarka ahaa. Wasaaraddu waxay ugu dambeyn ku dhawaaqday inaysan u aqoonsanayn go’aankii Maxkamadda Sare ee 5-tii November inuu yahay go’aan sharci ah, iyadoo ku doodday in go’aannada maxkamadeed ay soo saari karaan oo keliya garsoorayaal ku shaqeynaya guddi sharciyad leh oo uu hoggaaminayo guddoomiye si waafaqsan sharciga xilka u haya. Khubarada QM ayaa ku baaqay in xilka loo soo celiyo, iyagoo sheegay in xil ka qaadista aan loo marin habraacyadii dastuuriga ahaa. football.summary: يواصل فريق المريخ السوداني، الأول والرديف، استعداداته لاستئناف الدوري الرواندي والدوري الممتاز السوداني بعد فترة التوقف الدولي. جاء ذلك عقب إقصاء الفريق من دوري أبطال أفريقيا. الفريق الرديف أنهى معسكره في الإسماعيلية المصرية، حيث خاض عدة مباريات تجريبية. نفى مصدر في إدارة النادي الشائعات حول تغيير المدرب، مؤكدًا استمرار المدرب الملغاشي روموالد راكوتوندربي في قيادة الفريق الرديف، بينما سيستمر جندي نميري في قيادة الفريق الأول في الدوري الرواندي. الإدارة حددت يوم 20 نوفمبر موعدًا لعودة الفريق الرديف إلى السودان، حيث سيبدأ مشواره في الدوري الممتاز بمواجهة فريق كوبر في 25 من الشهر. كما أكدت الإدارة أنها تتريث في اختيار مدير رياضي ومدرب أجنبي لضمان اتخاذ قرارات مدروسة، مع وضع خطط لضمان ظهور قوي في الدوريين الرواندي والسوداني.
